narr: A couple of microbursts occurred in association with intense thunderstorm cells that formed in the heat of the afternoon. The storms developed during the heat of the afternoon ahead of a strong cold front that trailed south-southwest from southern Minnesota to extreme eastern Kansas. An increasing southwest low-level flow of moist and unstable air provided fuel for the storms. The storms evolved into a small but slow-moving complex over the Pennyrile region of west Kentucky. This complex produced very heavy rainfall that resulted in isolated flash flooding.
ev: About six miles southeast of Crofton, flash flooding caused a basement wall of a house to collapse, causing the entire house to collapse. Rescue personnel could not reach the site due to high water. One mile east of Crofton, a creek was out of its banks and over Highway 800.
